name: Structure and function of the heart

questions.q: What is the primary function of the human heart in the circulatory system?
a: To produce red blood cells for oxygen transport
To act as a muscular pump that drives blood through blood vessels
To filter out toxic waste products from blood plasma
To exchange carbon dioxide directly with the atmosphere

questions.q: Which chambers are known as the upper receiving chambers of the heart?
a: Ventricles
Aortas
Atria (singular: atrium)
Vena cava

questions.q: Which chambers are known as the lower pumping chambers of the heart?
a: Atria
Ventricles
Capillaries
Vena cava

questions.q: What is the wall of muscle that separates the left and right sides of the heart called?
a: The valve
The septum
The pericardium
The aorta

questions.q: Why is it important that the septum completely separates the left and right sides of the heart?
a: It prevents oxygenated and deoxygenated blood from mixing
It allows blood to flow backward into the lungs
It doubles the speed of heart contractions
It stores extra oxygen for emergency use

questions.q: Which blood vessel brings deoxygenated blood from the upper and lower body back to the right atrium?
a: Pulmonary vein
Aorta
Vena cava
Coronary artery

questions.q: Which blood vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs?
a: Pulmonary artery
Pulmonary vein
Aorta
Carotid artery

questions.q: Which blood vessels return oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the left atrium?
a: Pulmonary arteries
Pulmonary veins
Superior vena cava
Aorta

questions.q: Which major artery pumps oxygenated blood from the left ventricle out to the rest of the body?
a: Pulmonary artery
Vena cava
Aorta
Jugular vein

questions.q: What is the main function of the valves located between the atria and ventricles?
a: To generate electrical impulses for heartbeats
To prevent blood from flowing backward into the atria when ventricles contract
To filter bacteria from the blood
To speed up blood flow into capillaries

questions.q: Why does the left ventricle have a much thicker muscular wall than the right ventricle?
a: It has to pump blood through the whole body, whereas the right ventricle only pumps to the nearby lungs
It has to hold a larger volume of blood at all times
It receives blood directly from the lungs under extremely high pressure
It contains more valves to regulate flow

questions.q: What is the name of the specialized blood vessels that supply the heart muscle tissue itself with oxygen and glucose?
a: Pulmonary vessels
Coronary arteries
Jugular veins
Renal arteries

questions.q: What happens when the coronary arteries become blocked by fatty plaque deposits?
a: The heart beats twice as fast
Heart muscle cells are deprived of oxygen, which can lead to a heart attack
Blood flows backward into the lungs
The heart turns into bone tissue

questions.q: What physical sound does a stethoscope typically detect when listening to a healthy beating heart?
a: The sound of air rushing through the lungs
The 'lub-dub' sound of heart valves snapping shut
The scraping of bones against the pericardium
The friction of blood rubbing against capillary walls

questions.q: What term describes the phase of the heartbeat cycle when the heart muscle relaxes and chambers fill with blood?
a: Systole
Diastole
Pulse
Diffusion

questions.q: What term describes the phase of the heartbeat cycle when the heart muscle contracts to pump blood out?
a: Systole
Diastole
Respiration
Osmosis

questions.q: How does regular physical exercise affect the heart structure over time?
a: It weakens the heart muscle fibers and reduces capacity
It strengthens and slightly enlarges the heart muscle, making it more efficient
It stops the heart from beating during sleep
It turns soft muscle tissue into rigid cartilage

questions.q: Which of the following lifestyle choices increases the risk of heart disease?
a: Eating a diet high in saturated fats and leading a sedentary lifestyle
Eating plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables
Engaging in regular aerobic sports and exercise
Drinking clean water and maintaining proper hydration

questions.q: What is the average resting heart rate for a healthy human adult approximately?
a: 20 to 30 beats per minute
70 to 80 beats per minute
150 to 180 beats per minute
300 to 350 beats per minute

questions.q: What happens to a person's heart rate during strenuous physical activity such as running?
a: It decreases to conserve energy
It stays completely constant
It increases to deliver more oxygen and glucose to working muscles
It stops completely for short intervals

questions.q: Which side of the human heart handles deoxygenated blood exclusively?
a: The left side
The right side
Both sides equally
Neither side

questions.q: Which side of the human heart handles oxygenated blood exclusively?
a: The right side
The left side
The center partition only
None of the chambers

questions.q: What is the function of the pericardium, the sac surrounding the heart?
a: To pump blood into the aorta
To protect the heart and reduce friction against surrounding organs as it beats
To produce red blood cells
To filter waste gases from blood

questions.q: Why are semilunar valves positioned at the bases of the pulmonary artery and aorta?
a: To stop blood from flowing backward into the ventricles after they contract
To mix oxygen and carbon dioxide together
To speed up blood flow into the lungs
To anchor the heart inside the chest cavity

questions.q: If a valve in the heart fails to close properly, what condition or symptom might occur?
a: Blood leaks backward (regurgitation), making the heart work less efficiently
The heart stops beating permanently within seconds
Blood turns completely solid inside the chambers
The lungs fill up with digestive juices

questions.q: Which gas enters the pulmonary veins from the lungs?
a: Carbon dioxide
Nitrogen
Oxygen
Methane

questions.q: Which gas is carried by the vena cava into the right side of the heart?
a: High concentrations of oxygen
High concentrations of carbon dioxide
Pure hydrogen gas
Water vapor only

questions.q: What triggers the heart muscle to contract in a regular rhythm?
a: Electrical impulses generated by a natural pacemaker region within the heart
Conscious decisions made by the brain's frontal lobe
Digestive hormones released by the stomach
Physical gravity pulling on blood cells

questions.q: What is the medical term for a heart rate that is unusually slow (e.g., below 60 bpm in resting adults)?
a: Tachycardia
Bradycardia
Hypertension
Anemia

questions.q: What is the medical term for a heart rate that is unusually fast at rest?
a: Bradycardia
Tachycardia
Arthritis
Leukemia

questions.q: How do heart cells receive their own supply of nutrients and oxygen since they cannot absorb them directly from the blood inside their chambers?
a: Through the branching network of coronary blood vessels embedded in the heart muscle
By absorbing them straight through the outer chest skin
By digesting the walls of the ventricles
Through hollow nerve cords attached to the spine

questions.q: What role do pacemaker cells play in the heart?
a: They pump blood directly into the aorta
They generate electrical signals that set the rhythm for heart contractions
They act as one-way valves to stop backflow
They produce white blood cells

questions.q: Which factor can cause temporary increases in heart rate even when a person is sitting still?
a: Stress, anxiety, or release of adrenaline
Sleeping deeply in a dark room
Drinking a glass of pure water
Low room temperature

questions.q: Why is the human circulatory system referred to as a 'double circulatory system'?
a: Blood flows through the heart twice during each complete circuit of the body (pulmonary and systemic circuits)
The heart has two separate sets of lungs attached
Blood travels in two opposite directions inside the same artery
The heart beats two times for every breath taken

questions.q: What is cardiac output?
a: The total volume of blood pumped by each ventricle per minute
The number of breaths a person takes in one minute
The pressure of blood against artery walls
The speed of red blood cells through capillaries

questions.q: Which of these lifestyle changes helps prevent cardiovascular disease?
a: Smoking regularly
Eating a balanced diet low in saturated fats and exercising daily
Avoiding all physical activity to rest the heart
Consuming high amounts of sugary soft drinks

questions.q: What happens during a ventricular systole?
a: The ventricles contract, pumping blood into the pulmonary artery and aorta
The ventricles relax and fill with blood from the atria
The heart stops beating completely
Blood flows backward into the veins

questions.q: Which tissue type makes up the vast majority of the heart's thick walls?
a: Skeletal muscle
Cardiac muscle
Smooth muscle
Epithelial tissue

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of heart valves snapping shut?
a: To create the pulse felt in the wrist
To prevent the reverse flow of blood between heart contractions
To generate body heat
To filter impurities out of plasma

questions.q: Why is a healthy supply of blood to the heart muscle critical for survival?
a: Heart muscle cells respire continuously and die quickly if deprived of oxygen and glucose
Heart tissue can regenerate new chambers instantly if damaged
The heart does not need oxygen, only water
Blood inside the heart chambers nourishes the muscle directly through the walls
